source: NHTSA Vehicle Crash Test Database (public domain, US government)
summary: NHTSA research oblique: the 2,490.7 kg NHTSA research MDB 2010B (RMDB) at 89.68 km/h, towed straight (no crab), into the standing 2012 Camry (1,758.5 kg) turned 15 deg to its path, 35 % overlap on the car's LEFT front (report p.3, p.6, p.8). Films: 1000 fps off-board, 500 fps onboard, burned-in time with first contact at frame 50 (onboard 25). The face reaches the front wheel by 40 ms and the A-pillar base by 60 ms; closing speed along the RMDB's travel reaches 0 at 75 ms (sensors); the car leaves rearward and to its right at 15.4 m/s along the RMDB's travel, the RMDB at 14.1 m/s. Static crush 551 mm at C2 (C1 unrecoverable), bumper beam 613 mm at B2, left wheelbase -150 mm, RMDB face 308.7 mm. Proposed Rubble setup: engine/docs/crash-reference/scenarios/camry-oblique-left-mdb214.json (a stand-in: the FMVSS 214 barrier, 1,367.6 kg; see camry-oblique-comparison.md). The API's maximum crush 3,326 mm is C1's pre-test distance, not a crush.
sources: p.8 crash vehicle summary (masses, speeds, crush, offsets)

timing: t0_frame: the film frame (0-based, as the sheets stamp it; the burned-in 'Frame' is 1-based) whose burned-in time is within 0.5 ms of 0, the lab's first contact; ms = (frame - t0_frame) * 1000 / fps_film to within that.
